title: perf-bench-scratch-lena-park-2026-03-05
content:
Purpose:
- Quick scratchpad for latency/throughput runs on recent kernel changes (dynamic batching + KV-cache reuse).
- Save raw numbers, short analysis, next steps.

Test environment:
- Model: redwood-rlhf-7b-instruct (float16 runtime profile)
- Hardware: A100 80GB (single GPU) and H100 80GB (single GPU) for comparison
- Runtime build: serving-runtime@pr-456 (kernels: attention-opt-v2, batching: dynamic, kv-cache reuse enabled)
- Client harness: local runner (python) -> grpc -> runtime, warm-up: 20 requests, measurement window: 5 minutes
- Tokenization: BPE, average input prompt ~60 tokens, average generated continuation 256 tokens (config: max_new_tokens=256, top_p=0.9, temp=0.2)

Commands used (for reproducibility):
- python perf/run.py --model rrlhf-7b --device cuda:0 --batch 1 --seq 512 --iters 300 --warmup 20
- python perf/run.py --batch 4 --batch 8 --batch 16 (same flags)

Notes on measurement:
- Reported numbers: median_latency_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, tokens_per_second (generated tokens / wall_time)
- Warm vs cold: first request (cold) excluded from metrics; observed cold-start ~400-600ms (jit+cuda alloc)

Results (A100, float16, warm):
- Seq=512, batch=1: median=78ms, p95=120ms, p99=165ms, throughput=320 tok/s
- Seq=512, batch=4: median=120ms, p95=220ms, p99=340ms, throughput=980 tok/s
- Seq=512, batch=8: median=210ms, p95=380ms, p99=610ms, throughput=1800 tok/s
- Seq=512, batch=16: median=410ms, p95=720ms, p99=1.1s, throughput=2600 tok/s

Results (H100, float16, warm):
- Seq=512, batch=1: median=60ms, p95=95ms, p99=140ms, throughput=420 tok/s
- Seq=512, batch=4: median=95ms, p95=170ms, p99=260ms, throughput=1200 tok/s
- Seq=512, batch=8: median=165ms, p95=300ms, p99=480ms, throughput=2200 tok/s
- Seq=512, batch=16: median=330ms, p95=620ms, p99=980ms, throughput=3200 tok/s

Observed patterns:
- Batching increases throughput roughly sublinearly: going from batch1->4 gives ~3x throughput; 4->8 ~1.8x. Diminishing returns due to attention kernel scaling and memory bandwidth.
- H100 provides ~1.25-1.4x better latency and throughput vs A100 on same config (consistent with newer tensor core optimizations).
- p99 tails grow significantly with large batch sizes (>=8) indicating stragglers from kernel scheduling + memcpy spikes.
- KV-cache reuse enabled: for repeated prefix generation (chat-like), avg latency drops by ~18% for long sessions (seq>1024) vs cold prefix recompute.

Quick microbench (sequence length sweep, A100, batch=4):
- seq=128: median=42ms, p95=70ms, throughput=1400 tok/s
- seq=256: median=68ms, p95=110ms, throughput=1050 tok/s
- seq=512: median=120ms, p95=220ms, throughput=980 tok/s
- seq=1024: median=240ms, p95=420ms, throughput=760 tok/s

Notes on variability / noise:
- Observed occasional 1s spikes at p99 for A100 batch=8 runs. Root cause suspects: CUDA context eviction on noisy node (investigate SRE scheduling) or page migration (host->device).
- Need longer runs (1h) to build stable p99. Current window (5m) ok for trends but noisy for tails.

Qualitative observations:
- Dynamic batching (current PR) helps a lot for bursty traffic: median latency for mixed small/big requests drops ~25% vs static batching. But dynamic batching increases jitter unless we limit max_batch_latency.
- KV-cache reuse is high ROI for chat workloads: big wins at seq>512, small overhead to maintain caches per-session. Need eviction policy for memory (LRU per-GPU).
- Quantization (int8) test (quick): throughput +1.9x, median latency -20%, but output quality needs manual eval (synthetic hallucination increase observed in a few prompts).

Action items / next steps:
- [ ] Run extended 1h stability runs for batch sizes 4/8/16 on both A100 and H100 (ticket: JIRA SRV-801)
- [ ] Add tracing around memcpy and kernel launches to root-cause p99 spikes (link to PR instrumentation: GH PR #456)
- [ ] Test dynamic batching max_batch_latency tradeoffs (choices: 2ms / 5ms / 10ms) in canary cluster
- [ ] Prototype LRU per-GPU KV eviction and measure memory footprint for 10k concurrent sessions
- [ ] Run small qual eval on int8 model outputs vs float16 for 200 prompt set (eval harness)

Quick conclusions (so far):
- For latency SLOs (p95 < 200ms) we should favor batch <=4 on A100 for typical gen lengths (~256-512). H100 gives more headroom to push to batch=8 while keeping p95 ~300ms.
- For cost-efficiency (throughput/cost) batch=8 or 16 is attractive on H100 but increases p99 risk; consider multi-tier routing: small-latency route (batch<=4, reserved capacity) + best-effort route (batch>=8, cheaper).

Scratch/observations to preserve:
- CPU-side tokenization jitter contributed ~5-10ms occasionally; consider moving tokenization into warm workers (pre-tokenize common prompts).
- Memory allocator tune (cudaMallocAsync) seems to reduce cold-start by ~150ms when enabled.

If anyone wants raw logs or CSVs: I saved per-run CSVs under my local perf/ folder (will upload to Confluence page after longer runs). Ping me or drop a note in #eng-perf if you want copies.

-- Lena
